response: The clearest premature assent was my initial lean toward recommending Vendor B before I had weighed the EU data-residency commitment — I assented to the impression cost-plus-CEO-endorsement implies recommend B. The false judgement that assent carried was that the $32k saving was a genuine good worth pursuing, and implicitly that keeping faith with the CEO preference mattered more than keeping faith with EU customers. I withheld assent successfully at the decisive point: instead of finalizing the cost-first lean, I re-examined at the same depth, resolved the obligation I had left open (the EU-customer circle), and reversed to do-not-recommend — proximity moved from habitual to principled once the assent was corrected. I also withheld assent to the framing that delivering an answer the CEO dislikes would reflect badly on me; the guardrail confirmed that issuing the honest recommendation is the appropriate act.
